Apple___Apple_scab.description: A fungal disease caused by Venturia inaequalis that produces olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves and scabby lesions on fruit.
quick_fixes: Remove and dispose of heavily infected leaves and fallen leaf litter.
Prune overcrowded branches to improve airflow and leaf drying.
Apply a labelled scab fungicide according to the product schedule.
prevention: Plant scab-resistant apple varieties where available.
Rake up and destroy fallen leaves at the end of the season.
Avoid overhead irrigation that keeps foliage wet for long periods.

Apple___Black_rot.description: A fungal disease caused by Botryosphaeria obtusa that rots fruit and causes frogeye leaf spots and branch cankers.
quick_fixes: Remove mummified fruit from the tree and the ground.
Cut out cankered branches well below the visible damage.
Apply a labelled fungicide during the growing season.
prevention: Prune annually to keep the canopy open and dry.
Remove dead wood and fruit mummies before spring.
Keep trees vigorous with balanced fertiliser and adequate water.

Apple___Cedar_apple_rust.description: A fungal disease caused by Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae that needs a juniper or cedar host to complete its life cycle.
quick_fixes: Remove nearby juniper and cedar hosts if practical.
Pick off galls and infected leaves where feasible.
Apply a labelled rust fungicide from bud break through early summer.
prevention: Choose rust-resistant apple cultivars.
Avoid planting apples close to junipers or cedars.
Monitor the alternate host for galls before spring rains.

Apple___healthy.description: The leaf shows no visible symptoms of disease or pest damage.
quick_fixes: Continue the current watering and feeding programme.
Keep the area around the tree free of fallen debris.
prevention: Inspect leaves and fruit regularly for early symptoms.
Prune annually to maintain airflow through the canopy.

Blueberry___healthy.description: The leaf shows no visible symptoms of disease or pest damage.
quick_fixes: Continue watering deeply and consistently.
Top up mulch around the base of the plant.
prevention: Keep soil pH in the acidic range of about 4.5 to 5.5.
Prune out old canes to encourage new growth and airflow.

Cherry_(including_sour)___Powdery_mildew.description: A fungal disease that coats young leaves and shoots with a white powdery growth and can distort new growth.
quick_fixes: Remove and dispose of distorted or heavily coated shoots.
Thin the canopy to increase airflow and sunlight penetration.
Apply a labelled sulphur or powdery mildew fungicide.
prevention: Avoid excess nitrogen that produces soft, susceptible growth.
Water at the base rather than over the foliage.
Monitor new growth during warm, humid weather.

Cherry_(including_sour)___healthy.description: The leaf shows no visible symptoms of disease or pest damage.
quick_fixes: Continue the current watering and feeding programme.
Clear fallen leaves and fruit from around the tree.
prevention: Prune in dry weather to limit infection of pruning wounds.
Inspect leaves regularly during humid periods.

Corn_(maize)___Cercospora_leaf_spot Gray.description: A fungal disease caused by Cercospora species that produces long rectangular grey to tan lesions running between leaf veins.
quick_fixes: Apply a labelled fungicide if lesions are spreading before tasselling.
Remove or incorporate heavily infected crop residue after harvest.
Maintain balanced nitrogen to reduce plant stress.
prevention: Rotate away from corn for at least one season.
Plant hybrids with gray leaf spot resistance.
Bury crop residue to reduce the fungal inoculum.

Corn_(maize)___Common_rust_.description: A fungal disease caused by Puccinia sorghi that produces small reddish-brown powdery pustules on both leaf surfaces.
quick_fixes: Apply a labelled fungicide if pustules appear early and spread quickly.
Keep the crop well watered to reduce stress.
Record affected areas for next season's rotation plan.
prevention: Plant rust-resistant corn hybrids.
Avoid very late planting that exposes young plants to high rust pressure.
Rotate crops and manage volunteer corn plants.

Corn_(maize)___Northern_Leaf_Blight.description: A fungal disease caused by Exserohilum turcicum that produces long cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions on the leaves.
quick_fixes: Apply a labelled fungicide when lesions reach the upper leaves.
Remove or incorporate infected residue after harvest.
Avoid overhead irrigation late in the day.
prevention: Plant hybrids with Northern leaf blight resistance.
Rotate to a non-host crop for at least one season.
Manage crop residue to reduce overwintering inoculum.

Corn_(maize)___healthy.description: The leaf shows no visible symptoms of disease or pest damage.
quick_fixes: Continue the current irrigation and fertiliser programme.
Scout neighbouring rows for early disease symptoms.
prevention: Rotate crops and manage residue each season.
Keep nitrogen and water balanced to avoid plant stress.

Grape___Black_rot.description: A fungal disease caused by Guignardia bidwellii that produces brown leaf spots and shrivels berries into hard black mummies.
quick_fixes: Remove mummified berries from vines and the ground.
Open up the canopy to improve airflow and drying.
Apply a labelled fungicide starting at bloom.
prevention: Prune and train vines to keep foliage off the ground.
Remove all fruit mummies during dormant pruning.
Avoid overhead irrigation during the growing season.

Grape___Esca_(Black_Measles).description: A complex wood disease of mature vines that causes tiger-stripe leaf symptoms, and eventually dead arms and black spotting on berries.
quick_fixes: Remove severely affected arms or vines with clean cuts.
Disinfect pruning tools between vines.
Apply a pruning wound protectant immediately after cutting.
prevention: Avoid large pruning wounds and prune in dry weather.
Remove and destroy dead wood from the vineyard.
Keep vines well balanced and avoid severe water stress.

Grape___Leaf_blight_(Isariopsis_Leaf_Spo.description: A fungal disease that produces brown angular spots on grape leaves and can cause premature leaf drop in humid conditions.
quick_fixes: Remove and dispose of infected leaves.
Improve canopy airflow through shoot thinning.
Apply a labelled fungicide if symptoms are spreading.
prevention: Keep the vineyard floor clear of fallen leaves.
Avoid overhead irrigation and prolonged leaf wetness.
Monitor the canopy during warm, humid weather.

Grape___healthy.description: The leaf shows no visible symptoms of disease or pest damage.
quick_fixes: Continue the current irrigation and canopy management.
Clear fallen leaves from around the vines.
prevention: Maintain an open canopy and good airflow.
Inspect leaves and fruit regularly through the season.

Orange___Haunglongbing_(Citrus_greening).description: A bacterial disease spread by the Asian citrus psyllid that causes blotchy mottled leaves, lopsided bitter fruit and gradual tree decline. There is no cure.
quick_fixes: Remove and destroy severely infected trees to limit spread.
Apply a labelled psyllid control programme in the grove.
Report suspected cases to the local plant health authority.
prevention: Plant only certified disease-free nursery stock.
Control Asian citrus psyllids with monitoring and approved treatments.
Inspect new growth regularly for mottling and psyllid activity.

Peach___Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas arboricola pv. pruni that causes small dark angular leaf spots, shot-holes and fruit blemishes.
quick_fixes: Remove heavily infected shoots during dry weather.
Avoid overhead irrigation and working among wet trees.
Apply a labelled copper spray within the permitted schedule.
prevention: Choose peach cultivars with bacterial spot resistance.
Keep trees vigorous but avoid excessive nitrogen.
Prune for airflow and dispose of infected prunings.

Peach___healthy.description: The leaf shows no visible symptoms of disease or pest damage.
quick_fixes: Continue the current watering and feeding programme.
Remove fallen leaves and fruit from around the tree.
prevention: Prune annually to maintain airflow through the canopy.
Inspect leaves for early spots after wet weather.

Pepper,_bell___Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas species that produces water-soaked spots turning brown with yellow halos on leaves and fruit.
quick_fixes: Remove and destroy infected leaves and fruit.
Apply a labelled copper-based bactericide as directed.
Stop overhead watering and water only at the base.
prevention: Rotate away from peppers, tomatoes and other solanaceous crops for two to three years.
Use certified disease-free seed and transplants.
Avoid handling plants when foliage is wet.

Pepper,_bell___healthy.description: The leaf shows no visible symptoms of disease or pest damage.
quick_fixes: Continue the current watering and feeding programme.
Check the undersides of leaves for early pest activity.
prevention: Water at the base to keep foliage dry.
Rotate beds each season and mulch to reduce splash.

Potato___Early_blight.description: A fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani that produces dark brown target-like spots on older leaves and can reduce yield.
quick_fixes: Remove and destroy badly affected lower leaves.
Apply a labelled fungicide from the first symptoms.
Keep plants adequately watered and fed to reduce stress.
prevention: Rotate away from potatoes and tomatoes for at least two years.
Mulch to prevent soil splash onto lower leaves.
Plant certified disease-free seed potatoes.

Potato___Late_blight.description: A fast-spreading disease caused by Phytophthora infestans that causes large water-soaked lesions, white mould on leaf undersides and rapid plant collapse.
quick_fixes: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately; do not compost them.
Apply a protectant fungicide to remaining healthy plants.
Harvest and store tubers only from unaffected plants.
prevention: Plant certified disease-free seed potatoes.
Avoid overhead irrigation and long periods of leaf wetness.
Monitor weather forecasts and treat preventively in high-risk periods.

Potato___healthy.description: The leaf shows no visible symptoms of disease or pest damage.
quick_fixes: Continue the current watering and hilling programme.
Scout neighbouring plants for early blight symptoms.
prevention: Rotate crops and use certified seed potatoes.
Water at the base and avoid evening irrigation.

Raspberry___healthy.description: The leaf shows no visible symptoms of disease or pest damage.
quick_fixes: Continue the current watering and feeding programme.
Tie canes to the trellis to keep them off the ground.
prevention: Prune out spent floricanes after harvest.
Keep the row narrow and well ventilated.

Soybean___healthy.description: The leaf shows no visible symptoms of disease or pest damage.
quick_fixes: Continue the current crop management programme.
Scout fields weekly for early disease or pest symptoms.
prevention: Rotate with a non-legume crop each season.
Keep fields weed-free to reduce alternative hosts.

Squash___Powdery_mildew.description: A fungal disease that covers leaves with white powdery patches and can reduce photosynthesis and fruit size.
quick_fixes: Remove and dispose of heavily affected leaves.
Apply a labelled sulphur, potassium bicarbonate or fungicide product.
Increase spacing so foliage dries quickly.
prevention: Choose powdery mildew resistant squash varieties.
Water at the base and avoid overhead irrigation.
Maintain good airflow around the plants.

Strawberry___Leaf_scorch.description: A fungal disease caused by Diplocarpon earlianum that produces small dark purple spots which merge and give leaves a scorched appearance.
quick_fixes: Remove and destroy infected leaves.
Thin plants so air can move through the bed.
Apply a labelled fungicide if symptoms continue to spread.
prevention: Renovate beds after harvest and remove old foliage.
Avoid overhead irrigation and keep foliage dry.
Use certified disease-free plants.

Strawberry___healthy.description: The leaf shows no visible symptoms of disease or pest damage.
quick_fixes: Continue the current watering and feeding programme.
Remove old and damaged leaves from the bed.
prevention: Keep plants spaced for airflow and dry foliage.
Inspect new growth regularly for spots.

Tomato___Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease caused by Xanthomonas species that produces small water-soaked spots turning dark brown with yellow halos on leaves and fruit.
quick_fixes: Remove and destroy infected leaves and fruit.
Apply a labelled copper-based product according to the label.
Stop overhead watering and avoid working among wet plants.
prevention: Use certified disease-free seed and transplants.
Rotate away from tomatoes and peppers for two to three years.
Disinfect tools and hands between plants.

Tomato___Early_blight.description: A fungal disease caused by Alternaria solani that produces dark brown concentric target-like spots, usually starting on older lower leaves.
quick_fixes: Remove severely affected leaves using clean tools.
Avoid wetting the foliage when watering.
Improve air circulation around the plants.
prevention: Keep the growing area clean.
Avoid overhead watering where possible.
Monitor new leaves for additional symptoms.

Tomato___Late_blight.description: A rapidly spreading disease caused by Phytophthora infestans that produces large greasy grey-green lesions with white mould on leaf undersides.
quick_fixes: Remove and destroy infected plants immediately; do not compost them.
Apply a protectant fungicide to remaining healthy plants.
Keep foliage dry and improve ventilation around plants.
prevention: Avoid overhead watering and evening irrigation.
Plant certified disease-free transplants.
Monitor weather and treat preventively during cool, wet periods.

Tomato___Leaf_Mold.description: A fungal disease favoured by high humidity that causes pale green to yellow patches on the upper leaf and olive-green mould underneath.
quick_fixes: Remove affected leaves and increase ventilation.
Reduce humidity by improving airflow and spacing.
Apply a labelled fungicide if conditions remain humid.
prevention: Keep greenhouse humidity below about 85 percent.
Water at the base and avoid wetting foliage.
Prune lower leaves to improve air movement.

Tomato___Septoria_leaf_spot.description: A fungal disease caused by Septoria lycopersici that produces small circular spots with grey centres and dark margins on lower leaves.
quick_fixes: Remove and destroy infected lower leaves.
Mulch the soil surface to prevent splash dispersal.
Apply a labelled fungicide if spots continue to spread.
prevention: Stake and prune plants for better airflow.
Rotate away from tomatoes for at least two years.
Avoid overhead irrigation and remove crop debris.

Tomato___Spider_mites Two-spotted_spider.description: A piercing-sucking mite that causes pale stippling on leaves, fine webbing and bronzing, and thrives in hot, dry conditions.
quick_fixes: Spray leaf undersides with water to disrupt mite colonies.
Apply insecticidal soap or a labelled miticide as directed.
Remove heavily infested leaves and dispose of them.
prevention: Avoid drought stress with consistent irrigation.
Encourage natural predators such as predatory mites.
Check leaf undersides regularly during hot, dry weather.

Tomato___Target_Spot.description: A fungal disease caused by Corynespora cassiicola that produces brown lesions with concentric rings on leaves, stems and fruit.
quick_fixes: Remove infected leaves and fruit from the plant and soil.
Improve airflow by pruning and spacing plants.
Apply a labelled fungicide if lesions are spreading.
prevention: Rotate away from tomatoes and other hosts.
Avoid overhead irrigation and long leaf wetness.
Remove crop debris at the end of the season.

Tomato___Tomato_Yellow_Leaf_Curl_Virus.description: A virus spread by whiteflies that causes upward curling, yellowing and stunting of leaves and severely reduces fruit set. There is no cure.
quick_fixes: Remove and destroy infected plants to reduce virus spread.
Control whiteflies with traps, soap sprays or approved products.
Do not save seed from affected plants.
prevention: Use resistant tomato varieties where available.
Use yellow sticky traps and screen greenhouse openings.
Control weeds that can harbour whiteflies around the crop.

Tomato___Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: A highly stable virus spread by contact and contaminated tools that causes mottled light and dark green leaves, distortion and stunting. There is no cure.
quick_fixes: Remove and destroy infected plants; do not compost them.
Disinfect tools and hands thoroughly between plants.
Avoid handling plants after using tobacco products.
prevention: Use resistant varieties and certified virus-free seed.
Disinfect pruning tools with a suitable product between plants.
Wash hands before working in the crop and control weeds.

Tomato___healthy.description: The model classified the submitted leaf as healthy.
quick_fixes: Continue appropriate watering.
Provide suitable sunlight and growing conditions.
prevention: Inspect leaves regularly.
Monitor the plant for changes in colour or growth.
